content:
As far as I can tell, the docs workflow has recurring issues along with the issue that https://verified-zkevm.github.io/ArkLib/ returns 404 (which I get semi regular pings about). I'm planning to tweak this slightly in the short term (between Cambridge and Devconnect let's say) to:

  • generate docs in the style of https://github.com/leanprover/doc-gen4;
  • have a separate (fixed/more robust) blueprint generation or other more legible documentation to improve the current one;
  • Get a domain name and set up a very basic website that can point to both and possibly more (todos, ...) better than what the current page does, https://physlean.com/ seems to be a good example to follow.
That seems good to me, sorry I didn’t notice website being down. Seems like the new workflow fails silently at this

https://verified-zkevm.github.io/ArkLib/blueprint/ still returns something, although I think it's out of date. It hasn't really mattered so far -- I've had doing this in mind for a while, it's just been at the bottom of the list of priorities -- since I don't think any of us actively working on ArkLib look at it, but since it came up twice this week ahead of the Cambridge workshop and more generally we're getting closer to something that can be shown/advertised, I figured it was as good a time as any to lok into tidying this up a bit.

Looking at some of logs for failed runs of the workflow it also seems like there are weird edge cases that come up , which is why I thought it may be worth it looking at it from scratch with the doc-gen4 workflow as well.
https://verified-zkevm.github.io/ArkLib/ now returns docs, ignoring a few errors that showed up for some lemmas
Was there a reference you used for the original blueprint workflow? trying to see if it might be possible to reduce the amount of dependencies.
also migrating the site over to arklib.org (pending dns records updating)
